problems.title: The current correctness guard preserves hallucinated labels
problems.source_location: Section 2.2.2, PDF p. 4; Appendix B.1, PDF p. 21; separate supplement PDF p. 8, printed p. 24.
claim: Section 2.2.2 and Appendix B.1 classify a response as typical or creative only after the correctness gate. The original supplementary evaluator overwrote hallucinated labels in its final novelty loop; the current author repository instead guards that loop.
analysis: In current src/labeling.py, any evaluator rejection assigns Hallucinated_Solution. Lines 131–138 run novelty assignment only when that label is absent. A response rejected by both judges therefore retains its hallucinated label. This directly removes the historical overwrite counterexample.
result: The historical supplementary defect is fixed in the current source. Which version produced the published measurements is not established, and no current labeling defect is asserted from this witness.
problems.impact_rationale: The latest guard blocks the precise overwrite witness, so this historical concern supplies no current issue severity.
problems.existing_correction_status: The author-released current source already contains the correctness-preserving guard.

problems.title: The binary APm column is not the same metric across the released evaluation strategies
problems.source_location: Section 4.3, PDF p. 7; Table 3, PDF p. 9; Appendix Tables 11–15, PDF pp. 28–30.
claim: Section 4.3, PDF p. 7, defines APm as macro Average Precision with equal class weights; Table 3 and Appendix Tables 11–15 use that heading for binary hallucination detection. The released evaluation strategies under src/evaluation_strategy use positive-class-only AP in some paths and the mean of classwise AP values in others.
analysis: For labels \((0,0,0,1)\) with tied class scores \((0.5,0.5)\), positive-class AP is \(0.25\), negative-class AP is \(0.75\), and macro AP is \(0.5\). These distinct quantities cannot share a macro-AP label without qualification. Perfect predictions give one under both conventions, so agreement on that control does not establish equivalence.
result: The current binary evaluation paths compute different AP quantities under a common macro-AP heading. Published table values have not been recomputed.
repair: Average the independently computed classwise AP values in every strategy, or explicitly label positive-class AP separately.
problems.impact_rationale: The tied-score calculation proves a local metric-definition mismatch; it does not establish a changed headline ranking.
problems.existing_correction_status: A local correction or qualification is proposed where specified; author adoption is not established.

problems.title: Prototype AUROC and AP discard the continuous distance ordering
problems.source_location: Sections 4.2–4.3, PDF p. 7; released prototype.py, lines 324–361.
claim: Section 4.2, p. 7, defines the prototype classifier using Euclidean distance to class center embeddings and the nearest class. Section 4.3 then reports AUROC and AP alongside F1. The later implementation’s prototype.py, lines 324-349 for multiclass and \(351\)-\(361\) for binary classification, passes one-hot predicted class labels to the ranking metrics. The MLP, XGBoost, and TabM strategies pass class probability scores.
analysis: One-hot class predictions discard the continuous prototype-distance ordering. Under standard tie credit their binary AUROC is \((\mathrm{TPR}+\mathrm{TNR})/2\). Two examples assigned the same class can still have different distances, so this evaluates a coarser score than the probability-ranking metrics used by other strategies. Hard-label AUROC itself remains defined.

For one-dimensional prototypes at \(0\) and \(1\), queries \(0.1,0.2,0.3,0.4\) with labels \(0,0,1,1\) all receive hard label \(0\). Hard-label AUROC and positive-class AP are both \(0.5\), whereas the score \(-|z-1|\) ranks both positives above both negatives and gives both values \(1\).
result: Supported metric-comparability clarification, not an assertion that hard-label ROC is undefined.
repair: Keep nearest-prototype labels for F1 and accuracy. To assess distance ranking, retain a class score such as \(s_c(z)=-\|z-\mu_c\|_2\) and use those scores for the classwise ROC/AP calculations, with the explicit averaging rule from Problem 2. ROC/AP depend on score order, so negative values themselves cause no problem. If normalized scores such as a distance softmax are chosen instead, specify that choice and any temperature fixed using reference/validation data. In multiclass settings, softmax normalization can alter a class’s one-versus-rest ranking; no equivalence between these different score constructions is asserted here.
problems.impact_rationale: Discarding distances changes the ranking metric even with identical class decisions; this limits cross-strategy metric interpretation without refuting the representation method.
problems.existing_correction_status: A local correction or qualification is proposed where specified; author adoption is not established.

problems.title: Released input datasets and generation requests do not identify the described final filtered experiment
problems.source_location: Sections 2.3–2.3.1, PDF p. 4; released final-input filtering and reference-cap path.
claim: Sections 2.3–2.3.1 describe a final extended set of \(4545\) problems, a disjoint \(29\)-problem REF and \(371\)-problem TEST split, and at most two supplied reference solutions for non-REF prompts. The current data files and generation loop are the corresponding author-released inputs.
analysis: The current AMC, AIME and AHSME JSON lists contain \(2228,935,1732\) records, totaling \(4895\), which is \(350\) above the stated final count. Equality of full problem text after whitespace normalization gives \(16\) AMC–TEST matching pairs and zero REF–TEST pairs. This checks released inputs, not an unavailable final experiment manifest.

Current generation_and_feature_extraction.py loops through every supplied reference count. A non-REF record with three solutions therefore permits \(k=3\); with three generations per reference count it requests \(9\) responses, including a third-reference prompt. The stated cap is not enforced in this loop.
result: The release does not identify the described final filtered corpus, and its default generation path permits more than two non-REF references. These findings do not prove overlap or excess references in the actual table-producing runs.
repair: Release the final filtered split manifest and apply the stated two-reference cap to non-REF requests. Preserve REF exceptions explicitly rather than deleting records solely to force a target count.
problems.impact_rationale: The count and loop discrepancies impair reproduction of the stated data protocol; actual evaluated overlap and changes to reported performance remain unestablished.
problems.existing_correction_status: A local correction or qualification is proposed where specified; author adoption is not established.

impact_rationale: The current guard clears the historical labeling defect. The remaining supported findings concern AP conventions, prototype-score resolution and reproduction of the filtered input protocol, without demonstrated damage to the central creativity-detection result.
